mcqs.question: Why does a gas not have a fixed shape?

options.A: Its particles are far apart and move freely, taking the shape of the container.
options.B: Its particles are tightly packed like in a solid.
options.C: Its particles are liquid and flow only on the surface.
options.D: Its particles are fixed in a rigid lattice.

mcqs.answer: Its particles are far apart and move freely, taking the shape of the container.
mcqs.explanation: Gas particles are spaced far apart and move in random directions. Because they are not bound to each other, they spread out to fill any container, so a gas has no fixed shape. Options B, C and D describe solids or liquids, not gases.

mcqs.question: Why does a gas not have a fixed volume?

options.A: Gas particles can be compressed because there is a lot of empty space between them.
options.B: Gas particles are rigid and cannot move closer together.
options.C: Gas particles are glued together, keeping the volume constant.
options.D: Gas particles are heavy and settle at the bottom of the container.

mcqs.answer: Gas particles can be compressed because there is a lot of empty space between them.
mcqs.explanation: In a gas, the particles are far apart, leaving large gaps. When pressure is applied, these gaps can be reduced, allowing the gas to change its volume. Options B, C and D describe properties of solids or liquids, not gases.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the property of gases that they fill any available space?

options.A: Gas particles spread out to occupy the entire container they are placed in.
options.B: Gas particles stay at the bottom of the container, leaving the upper part empty.
options.C: Gas particles form a fixed shape that matches the container’s walls.
options.D: Gas particles only occupy half of the container, leaving the rest empty.

mcqs.answer: Gas particles spread out to occupy the entire container they are placed in.
mcqs.explanation: A defining property of gases is that their particles move independently and spread until they occupy all the space available, regardless of the container’s size or shape. Options B, C and D are incorrect descriptions of gas behavior.

mcqs.question: When a valve is opened and air rushes out, which property of the gas allows it to move in this way?

options.A: Ability to flow, because gas particles can slide past each other.
options.B: Having a fixed shape that pushes the air out.
options.C: Having a fixed volume that forces the air to escape.
options.D: Incompressibility, which makes the gas expand rapidly.

mcqs.answer: Ability to flow, because gas particles can slide past each other.
mcqs.explanation: Gases can flow because their particles are not locked in place; they can move past one another, allowing the gas to move out of a container when a path is provided. Fixed shape or volume (options B and C) do not apply to gases, and gases are compressible, not incompressible (option D).

mcqs.question: Which of the following situations best illustrates the compressibility of a gas?

options.A: Pumping air into a bicycle tire makes the tire harder.

mcqs.answer: Pumping air into a bicycle tire makes the tire harder.
mcqs.explanation: When air is pumped into a tire, the gas particles are forced into a smaller space, showing that gases can be compressed. Boiling water (B) and melting ice (C) involve phase changes of liquids, while sand (D) is a solid and does not demonstrate gas compressibility.

mcqs.question: A child inflates one balloon with helium and another with ordinary air. Which statement correctly identifies the gases involved?

options.A: The first balloon contains helium, a gas lighter than air; the second contains air, a mixture of gases.
options.C: Both balloons contain solid particles that float.
options.D: Helium is a solid at room temperature, while air is a liquid.

mcqs.answer: The first balloon contains helium, a gas lighter than air; the second contains air, a mixture of gases.
mcqs.explanation: Helium is a single-element gas that is lighter than the mixture of gases that make up air (mainly nitrogen and oxygen). The other options incorrectly describe the state of these substances.

mcqs.question: Some students think gases have a fixed shape because they are "sticky". Which statement correctly clears this misconception?

options.A: Gases have no fixed shape because their particles move independently and spread out to fill the container.
options.B: Gases are sticky, so they cling to the walls and keep a shape.
options.C: Gases have a fixed shape just like solids.
options.D: Gases cannot fill a container because they are too light.

mcqs.answer: Gases have no fixed shape because their particles move independently and spread out to fill the container.
mcqs.explanation: The lack of a fixed shape in gases is due to the free, random motion of widely spaced particles, not because of stickiness. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect ideas about gas behavior.

mcqs.question: If a gas is placed in a larger container, what will happen to its volume and why?

options.A: Its volume will increase because gas particles spread to fill the larger space.
options.B: Its volume will stay the same because gases have a fixed volume.
options.C: Its volume will decrease because gas particles shrink when the container is larger.
options.D: Its volume will become zero because gases disappear in larger containers.

mcqs.answer: Its volume will increase because gas particles spread to fill the larger space.
mcqs.explanation: Gases expand to occupy any available space; when the container size increases, the gas particles move farther apart, increasing the gas's volume. Options B, C, and D contradict the fundamental property that gases have no fixed volume.
